exposure: Maternal serum high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-c) concentrations
cohort: The study included 2241 pregnant women recruited and followed from January 2014 to December 2017 in three hospitals in Beijing, China.
finding: Maternal serum HDL-c concentrations were inversely associated with neonatal birth weight at 24 and 36 gestational weeks, with higher concentrations at 36 weeks increasing the risk of SGA births and the HDL-c trend across pregnancy being associated with smaller neonatal size.
